title: 👑 Elite Challenge ⭐⭐⭐⭐: Master of the Village

questions.prompt: Three of these job names are built from a real verb plus the ending -er. Which one is NOT?

options.text: a builder
a farmer
a carpenter
a teacher

questions.explanation: A carpenter ends in the same three letters as the others, but there is no verb carpent in English: the word is learnt whole. Behind a builder stands the verb build, behind a farmer the verb farm, and behind a teacher the verb teach, so those three really do follow the rule.

questions.prompt: Read: "Amine tidies his room alone. Sarra and her sister tidy their room together." Which sentence is correct?

options.text: Amine and Sarra help each other.
Sarra and her sister help each other.
Sarra tidies her room alone.
Amine helps Sarra with her room.

questions.explanation: Only the two sisters work together, and help that goes in both directions at once is said with each other. The text puts Amine alone in his own room, so he helps nobody and nobody helps him, and it puts Sarra with her sister, so she is not alone.

questions.prompt: Read: "Street A is clean. Street B is cleaner than Street A. Street C is cleaner than Street B." Which sentence is correct?

options.text: Street A is the cleanest of the three.
Street B is cleaner than Street C.
Street B is the cleanest of the three.
Street C is the cleanest of the three.

questions.explanation: Follow the chain: C beats B, and B beats A, so C is above the other two and the superlative belongs to it. Street A is under both of them, Street B is only in the middle, and "Street B is cleaner than Street C" turns the second sentence of the text upside down.

questions.prompt: Your class writes its charter. Which line is a promise about the future, and not an order?

options.text: We will tidy our desks every Friday.
Clean the blackboard.
Don't walk in with dirty shoes.
Tidy your desk.

questions.explanation: A promise names who will do it and puts will before the bare verb: We will tidy our desks every Friday. The lines "Clean the blackboard" and "Tidy your desk" start straight with the bare verb and name nobody, so they are orders, and "Don't walk in with dirty shoes" is an order not to do something.

questions.prompt: Meriem says the two words school and house. Which sentence about the letter h in them is true?

options.text: You hear the h in both words.
You hear the h in neither word.
You hear the h in school but not in house.
You hear the h in house but not in school.

questions.explanation: In house the air is pushed out at the very start, so the sound is there; in school the h hides behind the c and the two letters make one sound, so the letter is written and the sound is missing. Saying that you hear it in both, in neither, or in school and not in house gets the two words the wrong way round.

questions.prompt: Sarra describes her uncle and his work. Which of these sentences is completely correct?

options.text: My uncle is a farm, and his field is the biggest in the village.
My uncle is a farmer, and his field is the biggest in the village.
My uncle is a farmer, and him field is the biggest in the village.
My uncle is a farmer, and his field is the bigest in the village.

questions.explanation: Three rules must hold at once: the person is the verb farm plus -er, the owner is one man so the word is his, and big doubles its last consonant before the ending. The word "a farm" names the place and not the man, "him field" uses the form that receives an action instead of the possessive his, and "the bigest" forgets the doubled consonant.
